items.title: Three-dimensional mapping of human lung fibrosis identifies spatial coupling between tissue microarchitecture and maladaptive repair states
items.by: Bell, J. A.; Robinson, S. K.; Pedley, R.; Ahuja, G.; Szmul, A.; Reddin, I.; Thomas, J.; Norman, J.; James, S.; Basford, P. J.; Barozi, V.; Bhattacharya, D.; Par
items.why: A preprint pairing 3D X-ray histology with spatial omics to build a volumetric atlas of human lung fibrosis. It is a good test of how tissue structure relates to cell states. Not peer reviewed, and several authors declare industry ties.
items.takeaway: The authors propose that collapse of the alveolar-capillary unit redirects repair toward mechanically stabilised fibrogenic niches. This is their model, not an established result.

items.title: MorphoANOVA: Dissecting Histology-Gene Expression Relationships in Spatial Transcriptomics
items.by: Chen, P.-W.; Yan, G.; Yu, S.; Li, J. J.
items.why: A statistical framework (preprint) that separates how much of a gene's spatial expression tracks H&E-derived morphology from what remains. It suits careful interpretation of spatial transcriptomics, and the authors link code on GitHub. Evidence so far is simulations plus human cortex and three HER2-positive breast cancer patients.
items.takeaway: It uses nested spatially varying coefficient models with sequential ANOVA to test slide-wide, location-specific and residual spatial components.

items.title: Where Does Alignment Emerge and What Does It Mean? A Closer Look at the Platonic Representation Hypothesis
items.why: A critical look at the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, asking where cross-modal alignment emerges and which baselines make similarity metrics interpretable. Representation-learning claims like this need such baselines. It is a workshop preprint, so treat the conclusions as provisional.
items.takeaway: The authors report that the capability-alignment trend persists for newer models when captions are clean and informative, and that alignment between same-modality models remains much higher than cross-modal alignment.

items.title: Curve Circuits
items.why: A Distill article by Chris Olah and colleagues that reverse-engineers a learned curve-detection algorithm from InceptionV1 weights.
items.takeaway: The authors use what they learned to hand-build an artificial network whose curve neurons approximate the natural ones.

items.title: But what is cross-entropy? | Compression is Intelligence Part 2
items.why: A visual explanation of cross-entropy from 3Blue1Brown. The excerpt has no content, so the video's length and depth are unchecked.

items.title: Diffusion Models for Video Generation
items.why: A technical survey of diffusion models for video: 3D U-Net and DiT architectures, and how pretrained image models are adapted to video. The post lists "What are Diffusion Models?" as a required pre-read, which is not part of this edition.
items.takeaway: The post covers training from scratch as well as inflating pretrained image models with temporal layers.

earlier.title: Stand-In Effects and Pooling Amplification: Lessons from Biological World Models for Testing Action Effects
earlier.by: Bowen Xu, Boyu Chen, Jiaying Li
earlier.why: Uses biological perturbation experiments to question a common test for whether action-conditioned world models respond to actions. It reports failures of a simple replace-the-actions diagnostic under autocorrelated designs, and registered tests on published world-model families. This is an arXiv preprint, and the full paper is 100 pages, so read the abstract and key sections first.
earlier.takeaway: The abstract reports a pooled test rejecting in 0 of 96 units of one diffusion world model where actions mattered. Mixtures fixed in advance reached the registered power bar in all 96.

earlier.title: Learning Deep Phylogeny Through Epistasis-Aware Geometry
earlier.by: Jason Lamanna, Erfan Mowlaei, Xinghua Shi, Sudhir Kumar, Vincenzo Carnevale
earlier.why: Asks how the latent geometry of a sequence VAE affects deep phylogenetic inference under epistasis, comparing Euclidean and Poincaré-ball versions. The first version is from April 2026 (revised 10 Nov), so I list it as canon rather than fresh. It is a preprint, and the simulation results are the authors' own.
earlier.takeaway: The abstract reports that the hyperbolic version matches or beats maximum likelihood on topology in simulations, while the Euclidean one is less accurate.

earlier.title: Teaching LLMs to Update Beliefs for Efficient Long-Horizon Interaction
earlier.why: Explains ABBEL, which supervises natural-language belief summaries so a model does not need its full interaction history. Its results are reported by the authors on a few environments, and the gains are modest.
earlier.takeaway: On CollabBench, the reconstruction-based belief grading recovers about half the gap to full context while using fewer peak tokens, per the post's table.
